lessons.title: Start here: Specialist hazards: radiation, explosives, diving, marine and rail
lessons.body:
# Specialist hazards: radiation, explosives, diving, marine and rail

This original VNDRLY course teaches decisions within the company safety program. Work through six lessons, their six checks, two worked scenarios and a 20-question final. All cases are fictional. No equipment operation is required to complete the online learning.

Each of the 26 questions requires a recorded answer. Completion requires a correct answer or explicit acknowledgment of the explanation and corrected answer after an error. Preserve the first-attempt score separately from the remediated score; a correction never rewrites what was first understood. Read the explanation, return to the relevant lesson and resolve uncertainty with the responsible supervisor. The course does not substitute for a site assessment, permit or employer authorization.

This is general specialist-interface AWARENESS only. Radiation work/source recovery, explosives handling/misfire response, commercial diving/rescue, marine operation/transfers and rail access/movement each require their own qualified authority, applicable licences, technical plan, practical assessment and employer/site permission. None is conferred by this course.

The linked references support the subject and identify source context. Client procedures are examples of client requirements, not universal law or endorsement of this course. Apply the governing jurisdiction and actual site procedure; no numerical technical limits or universal renewal interval are invented here.

## Primary reference context

[OSHA Commercial diving — separate specialist scope](https://www.osha.gov/commercial-diving). Read the reference within its stated scope. Company examples are not universal technical rules; regulatory applicability must be determined for the actual task and jurisdiction.

lessons.title: Lesson 1 - Separate awareness from specialist qualification
lessons.body:
Radiation, explosives, diving, marine and rail work have different technical authorities, legal frameworks, equipment and emergency needs. Grouping them in a company register helps identify specialist scope; it does not make them one competence. This lesson teaches interface awareness for workers, supervisors and reviewers.

Identify the actual activity precisely. Industrial radiography differs from operating a non-ionizing device; a diver's underwater inspection differs from a worker standing on a quay. The scope determines the specialist requirements. Do not accept a certificate that merely contains the same broad word.

The qualified specialist and responsible employer must establish the technical method and personnel requirements. A general safety reviewer verifies that the appropriate evidence and decisions exist without pretending to approve technical parameters outside their competence. Online awareness never supplies a licence, specialist practical qualification or permission to operate.

## Worked field example

A vendor offers radiographic inspection with only a generic company safety certificate.

The safe decision is to hold the specialist scope until the relevant technical authority, permissions, personnel and plan are verified. General safety learning does not establish specialist authorization or technical competence.

A useful field record is specific: A scope-specific specialist package reviewed by the appropriate qualified authority. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

A company service register can contain several specialist activities without every employee performing them. Map the actual role first: a scheduler arranging a radiography visit, a guard maintaining the site access boundary and a radiographer handling the device have different responsibilities. The scheduler and guard need interface awareness; neither becomes an authorized source operator from knowing the plan.

The evidence review should preserve that distinction. Verify the specialist organization and people for their actual technical scope, and verify the general workforce's understanding of boundaries and alarm routes. Do not issue a single specialist-qualified label to everyone who attended an awareness briefing.

Where a contract combines disciplines, name the separate authorities. A marine contractor may use commercial divers, rail transport and explosives subcontractors, but one company's broad experience does not establish every technical role. Confirm the relevant lower-tier arrangements and responsibilities before the affected activity begins.

lessons.title: Lesson 2 - Respect radiation boundaries and abnormal conditions
lessons.body:
Radiation work requires the relevant licensed or otherwise authorized organization and qualified personnel under the governing jurisdiction. The specialist establishes controlled areas, monitoring, access restrictions and abnormal-event arrangements for the particular operation. This course supplies no exposure limit or exclusion distance.

Workers near radiography must understand the announced restrictions and how to contact the specialist. Do not cross a barrier because no work is visibly happening. Radiation hazards may not be detectable by human senses. A quiet work area is not evidence that the source is secured.

If a source or device is suspected lost, damaged or not returned to its safe condition, keep clear and use the agreed alarm route. Do not retrieve or move it, adjust the boundary yourself or ask an unqualified guard to investigate. Only the appropriate specialist controls assessment and recovery.

## Worked field example

A radiography barrier blocks a shortcut and a worker sees no operator nearby.

The safe decision is to remain outside the boundary and contact the authorized radiography representative. Absence of visible activity does not establish that the radiation hazard is absent.

A useful field record is specific: A verified boundary briefing and communication route to the qualified radiation authority. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

For a radiography interface, the specialist establishes the work restrictions and how other people will be notified. Site coordination then ensures pedestrian routes, deliveries and simultaneous work do not defeat those restrictions. The general supervisor should know whom to call, what area is held and how a changed condition is escalated.

A barrier is not an invitation for a general worker to determine whether the source is exposed. Workers remain outside and contact the qualified authority. Do not use a personal impression, silence or a lack of visible equipment as clearance. Technical monitoring and source status belong to the authorized personnel and method.

If an abnormal condition is reported, preserve the boundary and give reliable observations from safety. Do not touch an unfamiliar device or carry it to an office for identification. Source recovery and radiation emergency actions require specialist arrangements beyond this course.

lessons.title: Lesson 3 - Leave explosives decisions with the qualified authority
lessons.body:
Explosives and blasting-related operations require the applicable specialist permissions, secure arrangements and qualified personnel. Confirm the actual activity: transport, storage, preparation, use and abnormal-event response are not interchangeable duties. A worker authorized for one stage is not automatically authorized for another.

The specialist plan addresses interfaces such as access, other work, ignition or initiation hazards and emergency arrangements. General crews follow the stated restrictions. This awareness course deliberately does not teach initiation, charge preparation, magazine design or misfire handling.

Treat a suspected misfire, damaged item or unknown explosive-related object as an abnormal specialist event. Keep people clear and notify the designated authority. Do not touch, dismantle or attempt to make it safe. Schedule pressure and familiarity with ordinary tools do not create explosives competence.

## Worked field example

A worker finds an unfamiliar item after specialist blasting and offers to move it out of a vehicle route.

The safe decision is to keep clear, restrict affected access and notify the explosives authority through the agreed process. An unknown explosive-related item requires specialist assessment rather than ordinary handling.

A useful field record is specific: A specialist-controlled abnormal-event response and maintained access restriction. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

Explosives controls begin before use and extend through storage, movement, preparation and abnormal-event response under the applicable authority. A person who is permitted to drive a vehicle does not automatically have permission to transport or handle its explosive cargo. The actual functions need separate verification.

General workers follow announced restrictions, stop conditions and communication rules from the specialist plan. They should report an unexpected object or changed activity without manipulating equipment or improvising protective measures. This course does not provide safe approach distances, initiation instructions or misfire waiting periods.

After the specialist work, release of an area follows the relevant technical authority and site process. The fact that a scheduled time has passed is not clearance. Workers should obtain the current instruction and report conflicting messages rather than choosing the one that allows work to continue fastest.

lessons.title: Lesson 4 - Do not turn swimming ability into diving competence
lessons.body:
Commercial diving needs a task-specific diving plan, qualified team, suitable equipment and emergency capability under applicable requirements. Water conditions, visibility, entanglement, energy sources and pressure differences can create severe hazards. A recreational qualification or good swimming ability does not establish competence for an industrial dive.

Coordinate the dive with operations. Pumps, intakes, discharges, vessel movement and adjacent work may affect the diver. The specialist authority identifies required isolations and controls and verifies them with the responsible operating roles. A general permit cannot replace that technical planning.

If a diver is in difficulty, activate the established diving emergency arrangements. Do not send a willing swimmer into the water. Rescue and treatment have specialist requirements, and an improvised second entry can create another casualty.

## Worked field example

A maintenance worker volunteers to inspect a submerged intake because they are a strong swimmer.

The safe decision is to hold the underwater task for the qualified commercial-diving authority and reviewed plan. Swimming ability does not control industrial diving hazards or establish team and rescue capability.

A useful field record is specific: A scope-specific diving plan with verified team, operational interfaces and emergency resources. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

A diving interface assessment should identify the operational systems that can affect the underwater work. Pumps, intakes, outfalls, vessel propulsion and other energy sources can create hazards that are not visible from the surface. The qualified diving authority and operating roles coordinate the required controls and verification.

The shore team must understand its assigned role and how to activate the diving emergency arrangement. Watching bubbles or keeping a telephone nearby does not establish a qualified standby or rescue function. Recreational equipment and experience are not automatically suitable for the industrial task.

ROV operation is a different technical method and should not be described as a diver qualification. It still requires competent planning for equipment, cables, energy and marine interfaces. Confirm which method is actually contracted and preserve the qualification boundary rather than assuming all subsea labels mean the same workforce.

lessons.title: Lesson 5 - Coordinate marine and rail interfaces
lessons.body:
Marine and rail operations require their own qualified operating authority. A site worker should know the limits of the area, movement restrictions, communication and emergency route. Do not assume ordinary road-traffic habits apply to a rail corridor or that working beside water is the same as working on a vessel.

For marine work, the competent plan addresses access, vessel movement, water exposure, transfer, weather and rescue interfaces as applicable. General crews must not improvise boarding or transfer methods. For rail work, the responsible rail authority establishes the applicable access and movement protection; a parked wagon or quiet track is not clearance.

Coordinate overlapping work before it starts. A crane movement, a delivery or an inspection can affect the specialist operating area. Stop at an uncertain boundary and contact the appropriate authority instead of relying on a driver or bystander who may not control the operation.

## Worked field example

A contractor proposes crossing a quiet rail siding between parked wagons to reach a work area.

The safe decision is to use the rail authority’s approved access and movement-protection arrangement. Quiet or stationary rail equipment does not establish authorized safe access.

A useful field record is specific: A rail-authority access decision and briefing covering the actual crossing and movement controls. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

Marine access and rail access each need their own current operating permission. A visitor inspecting a vessel may require an approved boarding arrangement and briefing without being a vessel operator. A consultant reviewing a rail yard drawing may remain entirely at a desk. Assign exposure-based learning to the actual activity rather than a keyword in the service name.

Where people enter an operating area, verify the relevant authority, route, movement restrictions and communication. A stationary ship, wagon or crane can change state. Do not rely on someone who is nearby but does not control that movement.

Emergency coordination also differs. A water rescue, vessel evacuation and rail incident can require specialist resources and access arrangements. General workers raise the alarm and follow their assigned safe actions; they do not improvise a crossover method because they hold an unrelated rescue or driving credential.

lessons.title: Lesson 6 - Review change without borrowing another discipline’s approval
lessons.body:
A change in location, equipment, personnel, material or surrounding operation can invalidate a specialist plan. Return it to the appropriate technical authority before relying on the original approval. Do not treat the most qualified person on site as qualified in every discipline.

Evidence should identify legal entity, specialist scope, applicable authority, personnel competence, equipment status, technical plan, interfaces and emergency capability. Verify authenticity and currency through the approved review process. Record exclusions and unresolved conditions rather than creating a broad specialist-ready label.

General workers can demonstrate boundary recognition, alarm and escalation in safe simulation. Technical operation, source recovery, explosives handling, diving, vessel duties and rail movement require separate specialist assessment and authorization. An awareness result can support interface readiness but must never be presented as those qualifications.

## Worked field example

A radiography crew changes equipment and location after its technical plan was reviewed.

The safe decision is to return the changed scope to the radiation authority and verify revised interfaces before release. Approval for one specialist configuration does not automatically cover a changed configuration.

A useful field record is specific: A specialist change review identifying equipment, location, boundaries and emergency arrangements. It records observed conditions and the decision, rather than treating a signature as proof that the safeguard existed.

## Detailed specialist-interface application

A safe awareness evaluation can present a changed specialist boundary and ask the learner to identify the correct authority and hold. It should not expose them to a live source, explosive item, uncontrolled water entry or rail movement. The assessor records the demonstrated recognition and escalation, not technical operation.

The technical records remain separate. Where a specialist's licence, equipment, personnel or method changes, the appropriate authority determines what must be reviewed and verified. A general training renewal does not restore an expired technical permission.

The final handover should make restrictions clear to other employers and shifts. State what is approved, what remains held and who can authorize change. Preserve source references and original evidence, while protecting sensitive security details. A broad safety-program score must never be used to override a specialist hold or claim that online awareness has qualified radiation, explosives, diving, marine or rail operations.

lessons.title: Two applied scenarios and worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Scenario 1

At a fictional construction site, a vendor proposes radiographic inspection beside a busy pedestrian route. Its evidence pack contains a general safety certificate and a procedure from another location. A project supervisor offers to choose the boundary and asks gate staff to move the barrier whenever a delivery arrives. Explain the correct approval and interface sequence.

### Worked solution

The radiography activity is held. The responsible organization verifies the relevant jurisdictional authorization and appropriately qualified personnel and equipment. The radiation authority reviews the actual location and establishes the technical controls and abnormal-event arrangements. The site authority coordinates the pedestrian and delivery interfaces so access restrictions are maintained. Gate staff are briefed on the boundary, communication and hold process; they do not decide when radiation restrictions may be moved. A plan from another location is supporting background at most, not approval of this configuration. A safe interface exercise can confirm communication, but it does not replace specialist technical verification. The release record identifies the actual scope and the people responsible for the technical and site decisions.

## Scenario 2

A fictional water intake needs inspection near a rail-served terminal. A general contractor offers a recreational diver and proposes using a quiet rail siding as access. The manager says the combined specialist-awareness course should cover both activities.

### Worked solution

The underwater inspection and rail access are treated as separate specialist scopes. The commercial-diving authority evaluates the actual task, team, equipment, operational hazards and emergency capability. The rail authority establishes permitted access and movement protection. Neither is inferred from quiet conditions or broad course completion. The site coordinates any shared constraints and confirms that one activity cannot undermine the other’s controls. If either arrangement cannot be verified, that affected work remains held. The record preserves the distinction between awareness, specialist qualification and operational authorization. No one enters the water or track area merely to obtain missing information.

lessons.title: Final assessment - 20 questions
lessons.body: Answer each question without consulting an answer key. There are 20 final questions in addition to six lesson checks. Incorrect responses require reading and explicitly acknowledging the explanation. Both the first-attempt and remediated results must remain visible. A written result establishes course learning only; the separate practical boundary still applies.

lessons.title: Finish - Practical evaluation and work authorization
lessons.body:
## What completion means

The company may record this course as learning evidence after all sections and 26 questions are completed correctly or through explicitly acknowledged remediation. Keep the original result, corrected result and acknowledgments separate. This is not an independent determination that company controls are implemented or effective.

## What must be assessed separately

This is general specialist-interface AWARENESS only. Radiation work/source recovery, explosives handling/misfire response, commercial diving/rescue, marine operation/transfers and rail access/movement each require their own qualified authority, applicable licences, technical plan, practical assessment and employer/site permission. None is conferred by this course.

A competent assessor must observe the applicable assigned actions in a controlled, representative exercise or permitted work setting. Record the actual task, conditions, equipment, limitations and observed performance, including any element not assessed. Resolve unsuccessful demonstrations before assignment. Do not create live danger to test recognition. The responsible employer and site retain their own authorization decisions.

Review learning and practical readiness when duties, methods, equipment or conditions change, after a relevant failure, and when governing requirements require it. This course establishes no universal renewal period. Preserve personal and clinical information through the appropriate restricted process.
